newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index closes down but small stocks up.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index closes down but small stocks up.

text.p: * Index ends 3.4 points down, or 0.10 pct, at 3,275.83
The Philippine equities market closed down on Wednesday for the third straight session as small cap issues continued to draw away money from the blue chips, traders said.
"Second and thirdliners are still the focus of the market. It doesn't look like there's a let-up," Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc, said.
Value of shares traded was at 2.5 billion pesos.
Despite the index's slight drop, gainers beat decliners 63 to 55 with 78 issues unchanged.

Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Philippine Asia Equity, said rotational buying seemed to have taken place on penny issues as retail players shifted from one tertiary stock to another on a daily basis.
"I'm really surprised as most of the time focus on penny issues does not last long. If you are a fund manager and you see this type of movement, it's nothing more than a distraction," Lozada added.
Five small issues rose close to the 50 percent ceiling set by the Philippine Stock Exchange, prompting the bourse to freeze their prices.

Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Securities, said the trend may hold for the rest of the week but aside from tertiary issues, attention may be focused on bidders for the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS), the country's biggest utility.
